tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H17): Depth-2 pair kernel: one wave at <= 36 MB, half the waves at 57-134 MB. Build rope_pair2 in kernel.cu alongside the r2 kernels: each 16-lane group handles heads (2hp, 2hp+1) at positions (2*s2, 2*s2+1): rows row0 = 2*(bhp)*S + 2*s2, row0+1, row0+S, row0+S+1, with the second position predicated off when 2*s2+1 == S (odd S). Group index g -> (bhp, s2) via a magic divisor for S2 = ceil(S/2) computed on the host; Q groups first, then K; requires H and Hkv even, else fall back to r2's paths. Issue all 8 x loads (nc, L1::no_allocate) and 4 table loads (two table rows) before any FMA; evict_last cache_hint stores; 128-thread CTAs (8 groups = 32 rows, 16 KB of x per CTA), __launch_bounds__(128, 8). Check with compile_b200 (nvcc, not NVRTC) that regs <= 64 and spills = 0; if it spills, try computing outputs in place or 96-thread CTAs. Knobs: occupancy cap 8 vs 6 CTAs/SM (dynamic smem padding with the r2 carve-out trick) and 128 vs 256 threads. Measure vs r2 with 3 interleaved repeats at 6.6, 15.8, 36, 57, 61, 102, 134, 269 MB (6.6 and 15.8 MB are expected to lose from too few CTAs; find the row threshold where depth-2 starts winning, probably 25-35k rows). Record the first-wave size: at 36 MB (35,160 rows) the grid is 1,099 CTAs vs 1,184 resident, a single wave. Then wire the best threshold into the dispatcher (depth-2 for R in [threshold, 140k], r2 pair/row elsewhere), run_tests, and if no workload is worse than +1% submit as the portal probe of H15/H17 even when the bench gain is only 0..-2%: the mechanism predicts the gain appears on the portal (36 MB +23% vs bench) and r2 already proved pairs are not amplified, so a null portal result here is informative too. Success: Bench -3% or better at 36 MB and no loss above +1% at 57-134 MB; or bench within +-1.5% at 36-134 MB and portal -4% or better at 36 MB with M geomean -2% (H17 supported, H15 narrowed to wave boundaries). Refuted if: Depth-2 is >= +2% slower than r2 at 36 and 57 MB on the bench at both occupancy caps, or bench-neutral and portal within +-1.5% at 36-61 MB (then depth and wave count are closed for #88; the portal penalty at M is something else). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Keep the kernel copy-like (memory-bound): the portal locks the SM clock lower than the test bench and penalises extra SM work per byte (the problem card). Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H11): L/M hint and pair-path dispatch: pair at S > 1536, table evict_last, plain x at >= 134 MB, evict_first x. Four knobs on the r2 code, each measured against unchanged r2 with 3 interleaved repeats per size (bench noise is 1%; report medians and the spread). (a) H3/H11: remove the S <= 1536 limit so the pair path runs at 354, 407, 612 and 2689 MB; also try rope_pair<256> (16 pairs, 32 rows per CTA) there, since 128 vs 256 threads tie for the row kernel at L. (b) H19: table loads via ld.global.nc.L2::cache_hint with a createpolicy evict_last policy (r1 saw -2.7% at 612 MB, -0.9% at 2689), tested at 322-2689 MB and at 134-269 MB. (c) H19: plain ld.global.v4 (no .nc, no no_allocate) on x for R >= 120k rows (134 MB and up), tested at 134, 269, 612, 2689 MB; keep nc below 134 MB where r1 measured -7% at 57 MB. (d) H16: x loads with ld.global.nc.L1::no_allocate.L2::cache_hint and a createpolicy fractional evict_first policy (verify the PTX form compiles with compile_b200; fall back to .L2::evict_first qualifier if cache_hint on .nc is rejected), tested at 36, 57, 134, 269, 612, 2689 MB. Then compose the best setting per size range into one dispatcher (shape-only rules), run compile_b200 for regs/spills on every kernel, run_tests, and submit if no workload is worse than +1% on the bench. In the design card list every hint per path (x, w, st) so the emulator can learn them. Report per-knob tables; a knob that is neutral on the bench but mechanism-plausible for the portal (a and b) may still be included if it never loses more than 0.5%. Success: Composite kernel at least -1.5% at 612 and 2689 MB and -1% at 134-269 MB on the bench with nothing worse than +1%; portal L geomean -2% or better (about +0.003), M -1%. Refuted if: (a) pair at L is >= +1.5% slower at 354-2689 MB in all three repeats and (b)+(c) are within +-0.7% (then H11 is closed on the bench side and only the portal probe of (a) remains); (d) worse than +1% at any M size closes H16. Experiment E3 (tests H18): Small-shape specialisation: S <= 256 table-in-L1 routing, 64-thread pairs at 6.6-16 MB, and the 2.2 MB floor decomposition. Part 1 (H18): for shapes with S <= 256 (tables 128-256 KB: workloads 6.6, 15.8 and 134 MB) compare three routings with 3 interleaved repeats: r2 padded pair (10 CTAs/SM, 124 KB L1), unpadded pair with default carve-out (12 CTAs/SM, full L1), and rope_row<128> (16 CTAs/SM, full L1). Also check whether the carve-out switch itself costs anything: time an empty 256-CTA kernel launched with PAIR_PAD_SMEM + 50% carve-out vs the same kernel with 0 smem, each immediately after a harness-style memset, 5 interleaved repeats. Part 2 (H6 at S): 64-thread pair CTAs (4 pairs, 8 rows) and 128-thread pairs at 2.2-15.8 MB vs r2 (2.2 MB currently takes the row path because R <= 4096; test the pair there too with 64-thread CTAs = 256 CTAs). Part 3 (H12, record only): decompose the 2.2 MB and 6.6 MB times on the bench: empty 1-CTA kernel, empty grid of r2's shape, loads-only (x + tables, result reduced into one predicated store), stores-only, full kernel; report each span so the fixed-cost model (launch floor, round trip, store drain) gets numbers. Wire any routing that wins by >= 2% on its workloads into the dispatcher (shape-only rules), run_tests, and submit only if at least one of the 6.6/15.8/134 MB workloads improves by >= 2% with nothing worse than +0.5%; otherwise record findings only. Expected value is small (+0.001-0.002); the session's main product is the measurements for H6/H12/H18. Success: A routing that is >= 2% faster at 6.6, 15.8 or 134 MB on the bench with no regression elsewhere, or a carve-out switch cost >= 0.15 us that can be removed; plus the floor decomposition recorded. Refuted if: All three routings within +-1% at 6.6, 15.8 and 134 MB, the carve-out switch within 0.05 us, and 64-thread pairs within +-1% at 2.2-15.8 MB: H18 closed, S-band CTA shape closed, 2.2 MB stays parked.
